title: The composition of two derived tensor functors is a derived tensor functor
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file dga.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general-algebra at source lines 5958-5975: for differential graded R-algebras (A,d), (B,d), (C,d), a dg (A,B)-bimodule N and a dg (B,C)-bimodule N', and under the standing assumption that the comparison map (equation-plain-versus-derived-algebras) is an isomorphism, the composition of the two derived tensor functors -tensor^L_A N and -tensor^L_B N' is isomorphic to -tensor^L_A N'' for the (A,C)-bimodule N'' = N tensor_B N' described in the proof. The proof at source lines 5977-6064 is a long reduction: first replace both bimodules by property-(P) representatives, then use the split admissible short exact sequences of the property-(P) filtrations and the exactness of the derived tensor functor on the resulting distinguished triangles to reduce the claim to a single graded piece, then resolve (A tensor_R B)_B by a property-(P) module and repeat the reduction along a second filtration, ending on the one map that by construction represents the assumed isomorphism. Nothing in the argument is deep, but the two nested reduction chains are what makes the lemma hard to read, and the statement itself only asserts the existence of the bimodule N''.
